blocks.text: Esther's second banquet becomes the turning point. When the king repeats his offer to grant her petition, she reveals the deadly plot against herself and her people. Upon his demand, she identifies Haman as the architect of this destruction. The king's fury propels the narrative toward its reversal. Haman's own gallows—constructed for Mordecai, whose loyal service to the king had been honored and publicly recognized—become the instrument of Haman's execution. The plot intended to eliminate Mordecai instead eliminates Haman, and the very structure he built as a monument to his revenge becomes his grave. This reversal, where the antagonist's scheme destroys its author, closes the chapter with the king's wrath appeased.
